name: Bun cha ca
summary: Fish cake in a broth Cổng thông tin điện tử tỉnh Bình Định says is simmered mainly from fish bone and fish head, with a chili sauce it calls particular to Binh Dinh. Báo Người Lao Động, 3 Apr 2019, says the broth is not pork bone, usually tuna or sailfish, and that the cake has no dill.
origin: Quy Nhon. The provincial portal gives the address as the city. Báo Người Lao Động places a bowl on Nguyễn Huệ.
texture: Báo Người Lao Động describes fried cake and steamed cake in the same bowl: soft and smooth from the round and steamed pieces, chewy from the fried piece.
taste: The provincial portal calls the broth gently sweet. Báo Người Lao Động says the tuna or sailfish bone broth is naturally sweet, rich, and not fishy, and the dip is chili sauce with pickled shallot.
howToEat: Dip the cake in the chili sauce. Báo Người Lao Động puts herbs in the bowl and a sip of broth with the cake.

That article's herbs are lettuce, shredded cabbage, a few banana-flower strands, bean sprouts, and mint. The provincial chả cá page adds chopped scallion and dill to the cake, which this article says the central cake does not have. Both stay.
A shop hour was not printed. Check on arrival.
where: Nguyễn Huệ, on the 3 Apr 2019 article. Number 26 is the museum, not a stall.
seoTitle: Bun cha ca — Quy Nhon fish-cake noodles
seoDescription: Quy Nhon bún chả cá is fish cake in a fish-bone broth, not pork bone. One account adds dill and one leaves it out. A price is Check on arrival.
